Lectio reconstruction, 6 September 2026. All processing is local.
Corpus: The Latin Library via CLTK lat_text_latin_library source snapshot.
https://github.com/cltk/lat_text_latin_library
Source license: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (see CORPUS.txt).
Modified: whitespace cleanup, paragraph segmentation, broad navigation labels and catalogue titles. Source spellings retained. These are source files/books, not a count of complete works; fragments, selections and editorial material occur. The Later filter includes unclassified material. No complete-corpus claim.
Dictionary: Charlton T. Lewis and Charles Short, A Latin Dictionary (1879).
Perseus Digital Library digitization, with funding from the National Endowment for the Humanities; JSON conversion by IohannesArnold.
https://github.com/IohannesArnold/lewis-short-json
https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/
Dictionary and transformed dictionary data: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/
Modified: alphabetical shards, stable IDs and normalized lookup index; all supplied entry fields and nested senses retained. Digitization errors may remain.
Morphology: CLTK lat_models_cltk, MIT (see MORPHOLOGY.txt).
https://github.com/cltk/lat_models_cltk
Modified: lookup normalization and lemma suffix removal. Candidates are not contextual parses.
Reading-only release: speech removed. Original model assets preserved in source recovery and Git. Dictionary presentation omits unreliable converter grammatical fields. All supplied senses retained.

Perseus Canonical Latin Literature: one Latin edition per catalogued work, CC BY-SA 4.0 (see PERSEUS_CANONICAL.txt). TEI markup was converted to reading passages; spelling and wording were retained. The repository describes itself as work in progress, so edition labels do not claim textual completeness or critical finality.
https://github.com/PerseusDL/canonical-latinLit

Modifications, 2026-09-16: Perseus editions were re-converted to reading text. Editors' notes, apparatus readings and manuscript sigla tables are omitted; verse lines, speakers and editorial brackets ([deleted], ⟨supplied⟩, … for gaps) are kept, and passages follow the edition's books, poems and scenes. In 535 Latin Library texts, 5,355 transcription errors have been corrected, either where the aligned Perseus edition of the same work confirms the reading or after reading each case in context (for example manihus → manibus, cumLaelio → cum Laelio, eita → exposita); every change is listed in corrections/latin-library-edition-fixes.tsv in the project repository.

Short definitions: William Whitaker's Words (dictionary DICTLINE and inflection tables INFLECTS), distributed by its author as a free program.
https://github.com/mk270/whitakers-words
Modified, 2026-09-17: every word form in the library was parsed in advance against Whitaker's stems and endings (with -que/-ne/-ve/-cum, pronoun suffixes such as -dam and -cumque, and shortened perfects such as amasti); dictionary forms and English parse labels are generated by Lectio; the entry for sum, which Whitaker's program supplies internally, was added with Lectio's own wording. Parses are candidates, not contextual analyses.
